sections.title: Mission & Identity
data: Naval Station Norfolk is the largest naval complex in the world, occupying Sewells Point where the Elizabeth River and the James meet the Chesapeake Bay. It is the center of gravity for the U.S. Atlantic Fleet.

Its 13 piers handle about 3,100 ship movements a year, from aircraft carriers and submarines to surface combatants and Military Sealift Command vessels, plus the air operations at the adjacent Chambers Field. For a huge share of the Navy, a Norfolk tour is simply part of the career.

source.label: Naval Station Norfolk (official); NAVFAC Norfolk NS

sections.title: Which Side of the Water? The Hampton Roads Commute

data.subtitle: Hampton Roads is a cluster of cities wrapped around the water. For a sailor at Norfolk, where you live decides whether your daily commute includes a tunnel, and the tunnels here are famous for traffic.
intro: The base sits at Sewells Point in north Norfolk, on the 'Southside' of Hampton Roads. The region is really several cities knit together by bridges and tunnels, so the neighborhood you pick sets your commute for the entire tour.

The single biggest factor is the Hampton Roads Bridge-Tunnel (HRBT) on Interstate 64, the link to the Peninsula. It is being widened, with contract completion set for 2027, and a backup there can stall the whole drive. Living on the Peninsula, in Hampton or Newport News, makes the HRBT part of your routine. Portsmouth and Suffolk usually mean a tolled tunnel instead.

recommendations.advice: Live in Norfolk itself. From Ghent the drive is about 17 minutes with no traffic, with no tunnel.
Virginia Beach (Kempsville) and Chesapeake (Greenbrier, Great Bridge) are about 25 to 35 minutes with no traffic, with no tunnel crossing.
The Downtown and Midtown tunnels are tolled: in 2026, $3.40 each way at peak times and $2.42 off-peak with E-ZPass, more without it. There is no military discount.
Hampton and Newport News can be more affordable, but a daily HRBT crossing through a work zone is the least predictable commute in the region.
NOAA expects 23 to 27 high-tide flood days at Sewells Point between May 2026 and April 2027. Look up any address in Virginia's VFRIS flood map and price flood insurance before you offer.

source.label: VDOT HRBT Expansion; Elizabeth River Crossings 2026 tolls; NOAA high tide flooding outlook

sections.title: Gates & Access
data: Gate 2 on Hampton Boulevard is open 24 hours. Other gates include 3A (from I-564), 4 (Bellinger Avenue), 5, 6, 10 and 22 (Granby Street), and their hours vary.
Visitors without a DoD ID need a visitor pass and a REAL ID-compliant ID, arranged through the installation's Visitor Control Center.
Gate hours and visitor requirements change, so confirm the current details on the official Naval Station Norfolk site before you go.

sections.title: On-Base Housing
data: On-base family housing at Naval Station Norfolk is privatized and run by Liberty Military Housing, which was called Lincoln Military Housing until 2021. Liberty lists more than 1,600 family homes for Naval Station Norfolk.
Ask the Navy Housing Service Center how to apply and what the current wait is: 757-445-2832 (toll-free 1-800-628-7510), 7924 14th Street, Norfolk, 7:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. on weekdays.

source.label: Liberty Military Housing, Naval Station Norfolk; Military OneSource housing

sections.title: Schools
data: There is no DoDEA district in Hampton Roads, so children attend the local civilian public schools. On and near the base, that is Norfolk Public Schools.

Because families spread across Norfolk, Virginia Beach, Chesapeake, Portsmouth, and Suffolk, and each city runs its own school division, your assigned schools depend entirely on your address. Confirm the division and campus for any neighborhood you are considering.

intro: Whether to rent or buy is the biggest money decision of most PCS moves, and the answer is mostly about how long you'll be here and how steady the local market is.
rent: Your tour is short (about two years or less) or your orders feel uncertain.
You want time to learn the area before committing to a neighborhood.
You'd rather not gamble on resale timing when you PCS out.
Your BAH comfortably covers rent in the areas you'd consider.
buy: You expect to be here three or more years.
You want to use your VA loan and build equity instead of paying rent.
The market is steady and you could rent the home out later if needed.
You've found a neighborhood and commute you're confident about.
data.bottom_line: There is no universal right answer. Run your BAH against the rent and home prices above, weigh your tour length and the local market, and talk to a lender and an agent who work with military families before you commit.

intro: The first month at a new duty station is mostly logistics. Knocking these out early makes everything else easier.

steps.title: Line up temporary lodging
steps.text: Book on-base lodging or a short-term rental before you arrive. You can claim Temporary Lodging Expense (TLE) for a limited number of days while you house-hunt.

steps.title: In-process and update DEERS
steps.text: Report to your unit and finance, and make sure DEERS and ID cards are current for every family member so TRICARE and base access work.

steps.title: Start with the Housing Office
steps.text: Check on-base availability and get the housing office's read on off-base neighborhoods before you sign anything.

steps.title: Register your vehicle and sort access
steps.text: Handle base access and vehicle registration, and learn the visitor-pass process for guests. Bring your registration and insurance.

steps.title: Enroll the kids in school
steps.text: Contact the gaining school district or DoDEA early and bring records and immunizations. The School Liaison Office can help with the transfer.

steps.title: Set up healthcare
steps.text: Update your TRICARE region and enrollment so you can be seen at the local military treatment facility or network providers.

data.q: Which side of the water should I live on?
data.a: Families who want a predictable drive usually live on the Southside without a tunnel: Norfolk, Virginia Beach or Chesapeake. See the commute section above.

The Downtown and Midtown tunnels between Portsmouth and Norfolk do: $3.40 at peak and $2.42 off-peak with E-ZPass in 2026, with no military discount. The HRBT's general lanes are free; it is being widened until 2027.
Liberty Military Housing (formerly Lincoln Military Housing). Call the Navy Housing Service Center at 757-445-2832.
Naval Station Norfolk is MHA VA298 (Norfolk/Portsmouth). Use the calculator above for your grade.
